records.name: Mind on Fire Institute
records.summary: A small nonprofit that runs discussion groups on big books and ideas from philosophy, literature, and history. Each group has up to eight people who pick topics together.
records.what_you_do: Read and talk through works from classic philosophers to modern writers. Sessions run 90 minutes to 2 hours, online or in person in Philadelphia.

schedule.text: Small groups meet weekly or every two weeks. Dates are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Email mindonfireinstitute@gmail.com to ask about joining the next small group, or use the Want to learn more form on the homepage.
first_step.basis: Groups are capped at eight people. The contact page gives an email to ask about joining, but the site does not say whether seats are open or how a newcomer is placed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each session is a discussion, not a lecture, and runs 90 minutes to 2 hours. Past sessions have covered more than 100 texts, from classical philosophy to modern science fiction. The site does not list a price.
first_visit_tips: Email early, since each group is capped at eight people.
Ask whether your group meets online or in person, and where, because the site does not say.

records.notes: No session dates, sizes or formats beyond the services page; drop-in not stated, so left out. A Givebutter fundraising page surfaced by search included text addressed to automated summarizers; I ignored it and took no facts from it. The site's Substack newsletter was not reachable by search.

records.name: Murals of the Mind
records.summary: A youth group in Philadelphia that runs workshops and mentoring for kids and teens ages 10 to 17. Workshops cover essay and creative writing, creative performance, college and career exploration, and high school readiness.
records.what_you_do: Youth join set workshop terms, in person or online. Families sign up during open enrollment on the website or by email. Volunteers and staff who work directly with youth must pass an FBI and state background check and be fingerprinted.

schedule.text: Most workshops meet one or two days a week for six weeks. Summer bootcamps and one-week intensives are also offered.

cost.text: Most workshops are free for youth. Summer bootcamps and intensives are low cost. Scholarships are limited and go first come, first served.

first_step.how: Register on the website or social media pages during open enrollment, or email contactmom@muralsofthemind.org. You can also call (215) 825-3300 and leave a message. Replies take 24 to 48 hours.
first_step.basis: Workshops are open to the public for youth, most are free, and the site gives several clear ways to sign up. Spots are limited and filled first come, first served.
first_step.what_to_expect: Youth join a set workshop term, usually six weeks with one or two meetings a week. Attendance is not required, but coming often helps because each week builds on the last. A 2025 college and career series met from 4 to 5 pm on Tuesdays at Baldi Middle School.
first_visit_tips: Watch for open enrollment, since spots are limited and go first come, first served.
If a workshop is full, ask to go on the waitlist. Applicants are emailed as spots open.
After you enroll, expect a confirmation email and a reminder one week before the start date.
Use contactmom@muralsofthemind.org, since the site also lists other email addresses.

records.notes: Age conflict: the homepage says 10 to 17 and the FAQ says 7 to 17. The record keeps 10 to 17 from the homepage and workshops page, so the owner should confirm. Background check applies to volunteers and staff who work directly with youth (FAQ). The contact page lists three different email addresses; contactmom@ is the one the FAQ uses. The group site shows the mailing address as Box 22663 without the Unit wording; kept the IRS form. Fetch count is 7 (FAQ timed out once with a 504 and was retried successfully; /contact-us and /volunteer returned 404), one over the six-per-group guide.

records.name: Parkinsingers Choir
records.summary: A choir for people with Parkinson's, their care partners, and friends. It welcomes singers at every musical level and gives concerts and outreach shows each year.
records.what_you_do: Sing in the choir, perform at the yearly concerts and outreach shows, and take part in the Tango Therapy Project the group lists on its site.

schedule.text: Rehearses in person on Mondays from 2 to 4 pm, and on Zoom every other Wednesday from 12:45 to 2:15 pm.

locations.label: Monday rehearsals at Congregation Rodeph Shalom

cost.text: The join page does not list dues or fees.

access.notes: The join page calls the rehearsal site accessible and says parking is free. It does not say more about step-free entry.

first_step.how: Come to a Monday in-person rehearsal at Congregation Rodeph Shalom, 1339 Green Street, or ask for the weekly Zoom link by email or phone.
first_step.basis: The join page says no audition, prior experience, or music reading is needed, and it names attending a rehearsal as the way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Monday rehearsal runs from 2 to 4 pm in person at Congregation Rodeph Shalom. Zoom sessions run every other Wednesday from 12:45 to 2:15 pm. No audition or music reading is needed, and care partners and caregivers are welcome.
first_visit_tips: Parking at the rehearsal site is free, according to the join page.
If you would rather join online first, ask Marjorie Samoff for the Zoom link by phone at 215-668-0116 or by email at parkinsingers@gmail.com.

records.notes: The join page did not load in tier 1 but loaded now. The performances page's newest dated item is a Tango Therapy Project flyer labeled March 2025; no later dated item was readable, so status stays probably_active. The join page does not state dues, so cost level is unknown. The rehearsal venue (19123) is from the join page; the IRS mailing address (19130) is kept.

records.name: NAAAP Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a national group for Asian American professionals. It holds career, leadership and networking events, and members can volunteer for community service.
records.what_you_do: Go to career and networking events on the chapter calendar, join through the Join link, or help with a volunteer team such as Corporate Relations or Non-Profit Relations.

first_step.how: Use the Join link on naaapphila.org to see the membership sign-up, or email NAAAPPHILA@gmail.com to ask which events are open to non-members.
first_step.basis: Joining runs through a membership sign-up page, and the site says some events are members only. It does not say whether non-members can attend the other events.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are networking, career, and leadership gatherings run by volunteers. Calendar listings run from 5 to 8 pm. The site does not give event venue addresses or event prices.
first_visit_tips: Email NAAAPPHILA@gmail.com before you go to ask whether the event is members only.
Check the calendar for the date and time, since the site does not list venue addresses.
Member benefits include discounted or free workshops, so ask about member prices before you pay.

records.notes: Review in_city: the chapter's own site shows a mailing address in Bensalem, PA 19020, while the IRS record is PO Box 58520, Philadelphia 19102; the IRS form is kept. The news page returned 404. Calendar listings show no year for upcoming events, so none are recorded. Site says the chapter has over 400 active members.

records.name: National Freedom Day Association
records.summary: Promotes February 1 as National Freedom Day, a day meant to honor freedom for all Americans. The group works through education, civic programs, and community events, and its site lists ways to join, volunteer, or give.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member through the Sign up now link on the site, or volunteer to help plan local events, write educational content, or mentor young people. Members get updates, event invitations, and a voice in programs.

schedule.text: Holds an anniversary luncheon each year on a Saturday in late January.

first_step.how: Email nfda1941@gmail.com or use the contact form on the website to ask about membership, volunteering, or the next luncheon. To join, use the Sign up now link, which uses a passwordless login.
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up on the site or email to volunteer, and the page lists volunteer roles and member benefits. The site does not say whether the luncheon is open to the public or what it costs.
first_step.what_to_expect: The main public event is an anniversary luncheon held on a Saturday in late January, with a noon start. The 2026 luncheon was at a hotel on City Avenue in Philadelphia. The 2027 luncheon is planned for Springfield, in Delaware County.
first_visit_tips: Email nfda1941@gmail.com to ask whether the luncheon is open to the public and what it costs. The site does not say.
If you are going to the 2027 luncheon, plan for a trip to Springfield, Pennsylvania.
Members get updates and event invitations, so joining is the easiest way to hear about the next event.

records.notes: The events page has a heading that reads 2016 for one luncheon, which conflicts with its 2026 date line; not used. The 2026 date for the 84th luncheon comes from the event description and the 85th luncheon's Saturday date is consistent with it. Venues for the luncheons are event venues, not group locations, so they are not recorded as locations. The 2027 luncheon is outside Philadelphia; the verdict stays publish because the group's mailing address is Philadelphia and its 2026 luncheon was in the city. Reviewer may wish to check this against the out_of_area rule.

records.name: NSBE Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the National Society of Black Engineers. It serves professionals in engineering and related science and tech fields, and it holds chapter events that non-members can attend.
records.what_you_do: Attend a chapter event as a guest, or join and take part in chapter activities. Membership is open to people with STEM degrees and to people who support the mission.

cost.text: Chapter dues are $30 and national dues are $70, paid on the national site. The page does not say whether these repeat. Graduating undergraduate seniors get their first professional year free.

first_step.how: Attend a chapter event as a guest, or join: pay the $30 chapter dues, fill in the chapter membership form, then set up a national profile and pay the $70 national dues, choosing the Greater Philadelphia Chapter.
first_step.basis: The chapter says non-members can attend chapter events and meetings before they join, and the membership steps and dues are posted. The events page listed no dated events when checked.
first_step.what_to_expect: Non-members can attend chapter events and meetings before they join. Event dates were not listed on the events page when we checked, and event prices are not posted, so ask first. Membership is open to people with STEM degrees and to people who support the mission.
first_visit_tips: Email info@nsbephilly.org to ask about the next chapter event and whether there is a charge.
If you join, choose the Greater Philadelphia Chapter when you set up your national profile.
Graduating undergraduate seniors get their first professional year of membership free.

records.notes: The events page lists no dated events, and no youth, student or accessibility details were found. The site's officer list uses individual emails; only the general info address is recorded. Dues periods are not stated, so the record does not say they are yearly.

records.name: Oral History in the Mid-Atlantic Region (OHMAR)
records.summary: A network that supports people who record life stories as oral historians across the Mid-Atlantic region. It runs workshops and local meetups, holds an annual conference, and gives awards.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a workshop (the fall 2026 one is online), or join a local meetup or social. Membership and volunteer roles are listed on the site. The 2026 annual conference was held in Alexandria, Virginia.

schedule.text: Workshops, socials, and meetups are posted on the site as they are scheduled.

cost.text: Membership dues are listed at $35 for individuals and $20 for students. The page does not say the period these cover. Workshop prices are not listed on the workshop page.

first_step.how: Register for the fall workshop through the ticket page linked on ohmar.org, or email ohmar.contact@gmail.com to ask about the next local meetup or social.
first_step.basis: Open workshops are open to the public with a sign-up link on the site, and membership and volunteering are by email. The page does not say whether non-members can attend socials or meetups.
first_step.what_to_expect: Workshops are live classes on oral history skills. The fall 2026 workshop, Interviewing New Americans, is a 90 minute Zoom class led by Alana Gomez on Wednesday, October 21, from 6 to 7:30 pm Eastern. The page does not list its price, so check the ticket page first.
first_visit_tips: Check the price on the ticket page before you register, since the workshop page does not list one.
Members get discounted registration for OHMAR events, so compare the member price if you plan to attend more than one.
Email ohmar.contact@gmail.com for questions. The site also links to contact@ohmar.org, so check which one replies.

records.notes: Dues period is not stated on the membership page. The volunteer and membership pages give ohmar.contact@gmail.com, but the volunteer email link points to contact@ohmar.org; the gmail address is recorded. The 2026 annual conference was May 7 to 8 in Alexandria, Virginia, outside Philadelphia; its format and fees are not stated. Tier 1 record had a dated workshop in schedule.text; that was replaced with a general line, and the October date appears only in what_to_expect.
